overview: Two forms of mechanical energy — one from motion, one from position or configuration.
genZNote: One is energy in action, the other is energy on standby.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: Energy possessed due to motion (KE = ½mv²).
aspects.valueB: Energy possessed due to position or configuration (e.g. PE = mgh for gravity).

aspects.label: Depends On
aspects.valueB: Mass, position/height (for gravitational PE), or deformation (for elastic PE).

aspects.label: Reference Point Needed?
aspects.valueA: No — always measured relative to a state of rest.
aspects.valueB: Yes — potential energy is defined relative to an arbitrarily chosen reference level.

aspects.label: Interconversion
aspects.valueA: Converts to potential energy as an object slows while rising.
aspects.valueB: Converts to kinetic energy as an object falls/accelerates.
